content.title: About
content.content: The egg white sandwich is a light, protein‑rich snack made with two slices of whole‑grain bread, a fluffy egg‑white omelet, lettuce, tomato, and a slice of low‑fat cheese. Egg whites provide high‑quality protein with minimal fat and cholesterol.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg whites are almost pure protein and contain virtually no fat.
Athletes and calorie‑conscious eaters often choose egg white sandwiches for their low energy density.
Cooking egg whites without added oil preserves most of their nutritional value.
Whole‑grain bread adds dietary fiber that supports digestion.
The combination of protein and complex carbs gives lasting satiety.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Egg whites contain all essential amino acids, helping muscle repair and supporting metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike whole eggs, egg whites have virtually no fat, making the sandwich suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Egg whites provide riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy production.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Lysosome and lactoferrin in egg whites have antibacterial properties.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: Fiber improves gut health and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg whites, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salty sauces or cheese are added, the sandwich can become high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Possible salmonella risk
items.content: Undercooked egg whites may carry a risk of salmonella; always cook until fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich warm, cut in half for easy handling. It’s perfect as a quick on‑the‑go snack. Add avocado, mustard, or a light yogurt spread for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage keep components separate: bread in a dry place, egg white filling refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: Monster Low Calorie is a near‑zero‑calorie energy drink containing about 10 kcal per 100 ml. It delivers the classic Monster flavor with taurine, caffeine, B‑vitamins and guarana extract, providing a quick energy boost without excess calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink belongs to the “Low Calorie” line created for calorie‑conscious consumers.
Caffeine content is roughly 32 mg per 100 ml, comparable to regular Monster.
It includes vitamin B12, which supports red blood cell formation.
Available in several flavors such as “Zero Sugar” and “Fruit Punch”.
Packaged in recyclable aluminum cans to reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Increased alertness
items.content: Caffeine and taurine stimulate the central nervous system, improving focus and reaction time.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: B‑vitamins help convert food into usable energy, promoting a more efficient metabolism.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Approximately 10 kcal per 100 ml allows for an energy boost without significantly raising daily caloric intake.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Guarana extract contains polyphenols that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Enhanced physical endurance
items.content: The combination of caffeine and taurine can reduce perceived fatigue during intense exercise.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Individuals sensitive to caffeine may experience anxiety, rapid heartbeat, or sleep disturbances.

items.title: Not for children or pregnant women
items.content: Due to high caffeine levels, the drink is not recommended for children, adolescents, pregnant or nursing women.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and diminish the efficacy of some sedatives.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Possible reactions to flavorings, colorants, or other additives used in the formula.

content.title: How to Consume
content.content: Drink Monster Low Calorie chilled, straight from the refrigerator. It is advisable to limit intake to 250 ml (one can) per occasion and avoid mixing with alcohol.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days for best quality.

content.title: About
content.content: Grilled cod is a tender white fish with a light smoky flavor. Cod lives in cold northern waters of the Atlantic and Pacific, is low in fat and high in protein, and provides B‑vitamins and essential minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod can grow over 1.5 m long and weigh more than 30 kg.
In the United States, cod is one of the most popular fish for frying and grilling.
Cod fillets contain very few bones, making them easy to prepare.
Cod is a staple in traditional Northern European dishes such as fish‑and‑chips and Scandinavian fish soups.
Grilling preserves a high proportion of beneficial omega‑3 fatty acids.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Cod contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cod supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and B6, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a good source of selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bones.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: While lower than in fatty fish, the omega‑3s in cod are retained during grilling and help heart health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to marine fish, including cod.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Cod caught in polluted waters can contain traces of mercury or cadmium; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions may lead to excess protein intake and strain kidneys in people with chronic kidney disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grilled cod is served hot, often drizzled with lemon, olive oil, and fresh herbs. It can be added to salads, pastas, rice dishes, or served as a main course with vegetable sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh cod fillets should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and used within 2 days. Frozen fillets store up to 6 months at –18 °C. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.

oatmeal-instant-fruit-flavored-no-added-.title: Instant Oatmeal, Fruit Flavored, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Instant fruit‑flavored oatmeal is a dry breakfast that can be prepared in 1–2 minutes by adding hot water or milk. It contains whole oat flakes, dried fruit pieces and natural flavorings, with no added fat. The product is convenient for travel, work and school.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for more than 5,000 years.
Instant oatmeal retains most of the dietary fiber found in regular rolled oats.
Fruit pieces are usually made from dried berries and fruits, preserving some vitamins and minerals.
The lack of added fat makes the product low‑calorie while still providing a feeling of fullness thanks to fiber.
Oatmeal is a common component of sports nutrition because of its slow‑release energy.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans can lower cholesterol and support the immune system.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 are involved in energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Fruit adds antioxidants
items.content: Dried berries and fruits provide vitamin C and polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added fat makes it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to oats or to the avenin protein they contain.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit flavorings can increase sugar levels; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on the same lines as wheat, so gluten cross‑contamination is possible.

items.title: Heat‑sensitive nutrients
items.content: Very hot water can degrade some vitamin C and certain polyphenols.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour about 40 g of oatmeal into a bowl, add hot water or milk, stir and let stand for 1–2 minutes. You can enhance it with nuts, seeds, yogurt or fresh fruit for extra nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed to prevent moisture absorption.

pasta-with-cream-sauce-and-seafood-resta.title: Pasta with Cream Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce and seafood is an Italian-inspired dish that combines al dente pasta, a silky cream sauce, and a mix of seafood such as shrimp, mussels, and calamari. The sauce is made from cream, white wine, garlic, and herbs, while the seafood is quickly sautéed to stay tender. The dish provides high‑quality protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The creamy sauce is often called “Alfredo” in the U.S., though the original Italian version differs.
Seafood is added at the end of cooking to prevent it from becoming rubbery.
Cream stabilizes aromatic compounds, giving the sauce a rounded flavor.
Traditionally the dish is finished with grated Parmesan, enhancing umami.
It is especially popular in coastal restaurants where fresh seafood is available daily.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Seafood such as shrimp and mussels provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood supplies EPA and DHA, which support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cream and some seafood (e.g., mussels) contribute calcium and vitamin D for strong bones.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Garlic and white wine add polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The cream sauce is rich in saturated fat and calories, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑watching diets.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauces and seafood are often salted; people with hypertension should limit added salt.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly stored seafood can harbor bacteria; it should be cooked and kept at proper temperatures.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta until al dente, reserve a cup of cooking water, then drain. Sauté the seafood in olive oil, add garlic, wine, and cream, and simmer until thickened. Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding a splash of the reserved water if needed. Top with grated Parmesan and fresh parsley, serve hot, and finish with a squeeze of lemon if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a little water or cream to restore sauce consistency. Freezing is not recommended, as the cream sauce may separate.

rice-brown-with-vegetables-soy-based-sau.title: Brown Rice with Vegetables and Soy Sauce (No Added Fat)

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product that retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice. This dish combines brown rice with a mix of vegetables (carrot, broccoli, bell pepper) and a soy‑based sauce, without any added fat. The combination provides a balanced mix of carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins, and plant protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice contains 3‑4 times more fiber than white rice.
Soy sauce originated in China over 2,500 years ago.
Vegetables retain most of their vitamins when steamed or quickly stir‑fried.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.
The lack of added fat makes the dish suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Soy sauce and vegetables add essential amino acids useful for muscle recovery.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Brown rice and vegetables provide thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added fat keeps the calorie count low, making it suitable for weight‑management plans.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables such as broccoli and bell pepper contain vitamin C and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Soy sauce can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to soy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Traditional soy sauce is salty; choose a low‑sodium version if you need to limit salt intake.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which may reduce mineral absorption when consumed in very large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish as a main meal or as a side to meat or fish. It reheats well in the microwave or on a skillet with a splash of water to prevent drying out. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, cilantro) or a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it can be stored for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat to at least 75 °C before eating.
